{{Short description|Mathematician}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''Barbara Trader Faires''' (born 1943) is an American mathematician who served as professor, department chair, and Vice President for Academic Affairs at [[Westminster College (Pennsylvania)|Westminster College]] in [[Pennsylvania]] and served for 8 years as Secretary<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://twitter.com/mathyawp/status/950887019026132992|title=Francis Su on Twitter|work=Twitter|access-date=2018-11-28|language=en}}</ref> of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] (MAA).<ref name="MAA">{{Cite web|url=https://www.maa.org/about-maa/governance/barbara-faires-maa-secretary|title=Barbara Faires - MAA Secretary {{!}} Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org|language=en|access-date=2018-11-28|archive-date=2019-04-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190420200513/https://www.maa.org/about-maa/governance/barbara-faires-maa-secretary|url-status=dead}}</ref> She received the Yueh-Gin Gung and Dr. Charles Y. Hu Award for Distinguished Service to Mathematics from the MAA in 2022.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Yueh-Gin Gung and Dr. Charles Y. Hu Award for 2022 to Barbara Faires for Distinguished Service to Mathematics |journal=American Mathematical Monthly |date=2022 |volume=129 |issue=7 |pages=603–607}}</ref> She is now retired and living in [[Pulaski Township, Lawrence County, Pennsylvania|Pulaski Township, Pennsylvania]].

Faires earned her undergraduate degree at [[East Carolina University]], double-majoring in mathematics and business.<ref name="MAA"/> She earned her doctorate at Kent State University in 1974; her dissertation title was "On [[Grothendieck space|Grothendieck Spaces]] and Vector Measures" and completed under the supervision of [[Joseph Diestel]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=11127}}</ref>   Faires extended her studies into computer science during a sabbatical leave at [[Carnegie Mellon University]] where she also had a visiting position. Another visiting position took her to [[Westminster College, Oxford|Westminster College]] in [[Oxford|Oxford, UK]].<ref name="MAA" />

She was married to mathematician J. Douglas Faires (1941-2012)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.vindy.com/news/tributes/2012/dec/30/j-douglas-faire/|title=J. DOUGLAS FAIRES|last=Vindicator|first=The|website=vindy.com|access-date=2018-12-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190420200516/http://www.vindy.com/news/tributes/2012/dec/30/j-douglas-faire/|archive-date=2019-04-20|url-status=dead}}</ref> who taught at nearby [[Youngstown State University|Youngstown University]] in [[Youngstown, Ohio]].  Together they authored several calculus textbooks.{{citation needed|date=April 2023}}
